source: docs/2026 LCY EHS Dash Board.xlsx (SHA-256 0B94C09BEDF3C343D3250496780A2D3B66671B55741ABA0391FDE81BE8B51C10), sheets 'Rates' and 'TRIR EXP.'
notes: Load with: python -m app.safety.performance.legacy_import check|plan|apply <this file>. Not applied by any migration.
Monthly hours are Rates!M (Monthly Hours Worked (Total)), typed values imported as stated. Rates!K (Hourly) and Rates!L (Salary) are blank for 2025 and 2026, so no breakdown is imported.
Rates!M17 (January 2025) = 15000 is a typed workbook value and is imported as stated.
The workbook does not state which workers Rates!M covers. It is stored as the site's total worked hours as typed; there is no contractor-hours field.

Closure is never inferred from hours being present: each closed month states its closedBasis. 2025 months close on the typed 2025 annual hours; closing a legacy month confirms the hours only, and blank 2025 counts in safety_performance_legacy_2025_lcy_ehs.mapping.json stay unconfirmed. 2026 months close as complete Incident & Near Miss months; confirm with the Safety owner before apply.
September 2026 hours (Rates!M37) are blank; September 2026 is not imported, stays Not Reported and open, and is excluded from every rate window.

CONFLICT (for separate Incident & Near Miss review, not changed here): Rates!E36 records 1 Lost Time Injury for August 2026, which Incident & Near Miss does not record. Safety Performance does not use Lost Time Injury and reads Incident & Near Miss as authoritative.

Annual rows are TRIR EXP. row 8 (Recordable) and row 15 (Man Hours) for years without monthly hours. Their stated TRIR (row 18) matches recordables x 200000 / hours. The BLS industry averages (row 19) are not imported.
